subject: Evaluation runbook & 10-day trial proposal — Olive.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluation runbook & 10-day trial proposal — Olive.ai

Hi Samira / Michael —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — appreciated the candid discussion about inference cost and the integration constraints you mentioned around hosting in your private VPC. I promised a concrete, timeboxed evaluation plan; attached is a short runbook (redwood-eval-runbook.xlsx) with success criteria, test datasets, and ownership. High level below: 

- Goal: Validate Redwood's inference economics and latency in a representative Olive.ai flow, and measure retrieval+generation fidelity on a 500-doc subset.
- Window: 10 full business days once sandbox access is provisioned.
- Success criteria (initial proposal):
  * Latency: p95 < 200ms for 512-token generation under expected concurrency (5 concurrent sessions)
  * Cost: tokens/unit cost projection within 20% of our estimate in the runbook
  * Quality: top-1 semantic relevance (embedding + rerank) > 0.84 on the provided eval set; no critical hallucination cases on the sample prompts
- Ownership: Karthik (sales) — timelines and commercial; Monica (SE) — technical setup and run; Laura (CS) — onboarding & success metrics.
- Needed from Olive.ai: sandbox API access or one-shot export of the 500-doc eval set, CORS/VPC connectivity window for private endpoint testing, and a primary point-of-contact for infra (we'll need to coordinate IP allowlisting).

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm success criteria and the eval window by EOD Wednesday, Oct 7.
2) If agreed, we schedule a 30-minute kickoff with your infra team for Thursday or Friday to get the sandbox endpoint and allowlist ready.
3) Monica will provision a temporary private endpoint / short-lived credentials and share test harness instructions.

I've attached a short security brief as well — happy to redline any of this with your security team. If this looks good, I can turn the runbook into a one-page SOW to attach to our trial paperwork.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0147

Subject: Re: Evaluation runbook & 10-day trial proposal — Olive.ai

Karthik —

Thanks for this. Quick notes from our side after reviewing the doc with Michael: 

- The 10-day window is fine, but we need the latency target clarified for cold-cache conditions. Our baseline includes cold-starts from an empty KV cache every morning — can you add expected cold and warm p95s?
- We cannot provide direct VPC peering for trial customers; the only option is a client-side tunnel (we can spin up an EC2 bastion) or use a limited-privilege proxy that Mazda team can host. Can you list the minimal ports/protocols needed for the testing runbook?
- We want one additional success metric focused on inference determinism for our logging pipeline: 95% identical outputs (top-1) on identical prompts across 5 runs (to detect non-deterministic sampling).

Also: security will need to review the redwood-security-brief — I'll loop in our security lead if needed. For now, we'll target a kickoff the week of Oct 12.

Samira
Director of ML Products | Olive.ai
samira@olive.ai

Hi Samira / Michael —

Thanks for the quick review and the determinism metric suggestion — good call. A couple of concrete answers and a slightly revised checklist (I'm attaching a small runbook section to the spreadsheet):

1) Cold vs warm p95s: for your target model family (LlamaV3-like 13B quantized), we expect cold p95 in a private tunneled setup ~300-350ms for 512 tokens (first request after cache eviction) and warm p95 ~120-180ms assuming a warmed KV cache and continuous traffic at 5 concurrent sessions. We'll instrument both during the run and report both figures separately.

2) Network ports/protocols: outbound TLS (443) from your bastion/proxy to our endpoint; websocket or HTTP/2 is fine for streaming. No inbound ports required on your infra; we can accept connections from your side (client-initiated). I added a short section to the runbook with the exact headers and sample curl commands.

3) Determinism: we'll add a determinism check in the harness (5 runs per prompt, top-1 exact-match rate). We'll record both cosine similarity and exact-match for deterministic signals. Proposed threshold: >=95% exact-match on canonical prompts + no more than 1 critical hallucination in the sample slice.

4) Data handling: we'll only stage the eval subset in an ephemeral store for the duration of the trial and redact PII fields. Full audit logs will be available to your security team on request (we provided the brief).

Next steps from our side: I can host the kickoff and run the initial warm-up scripts. Proposed kickoff: Tue, Oct 13 at 10:00 AM PT. If that works, I'll send calendar invites and a short SE-runbook doc.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
